input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs

## Description

Delivers a run comparison view in the Dashboard: users select two or more
training or Data Science Pipelines runs and view their parameters and metrics
side by side, including a diff presentation that highlights which parameters
and metrics changed between two selected runs. This gives data scientists
in-platform visibility for model promotion decisions, replacing the current
exported-spreadsheet workflow.

## Scope

- Multi-run selection from the runs list in the Dashboard, covering both
  training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs.
- Side-by-side rendering of parameters and metrics for the selected runs.
- Diff presentation over the same comparison surface: given two selected runs,
  highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them (unchanged
  values remain visible for context).
- The comparison consumes run parameters and metrics through the existing
  per-run data sources; no change to how runs record parameters or metrics.
- Passive validation of Data Science Pipelines: pipeline runs need no code
  change, and their continued correct operation is validated here — pipeline
  run parameters and metrics must render in the comparison with the same
  structure as training runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs selected from the runs list, when the user opens the
  comparison, then the parameters and metrics of all selected runs are
  displayed side by side in the Dashboard.
- Given two runs selected in the comparison, when the diff presentation is
  shown, then parameters and metrics that changed between the two runs are
  highlighted and distinguishable from unchanged ones.
- Given a selection that includes a Data Science Pipelines run, its parameters
  and metrics render in the comparison with the same structure as training
  runs (passive-component validation for Data Science Pipelines).
- The comparison is reachable from the runs list for both training runs and
  pipeline runs without leaving the Dashboard.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard — primary coverage.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled with HLR-1): the run "diff" view is a presentation mode
  of the same comparison surface over the same run data — one capability
  stated twice in wording consolidated from two customer councils. Bundled,
  not split: it shares the data structures, UI surface, and call sites of the
  side-by-side view, so a separate epic would build the same surface twice
  and is not separately schedulable.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record a reference to the run (training or pipeline
run) that produced them, and expose that reference through the Model Registry's
API so platform clients can resolve the producing run — for example, to open a
run comparison seeded with it.

## Scope

- Support recording of the producing-run reference on registered model
  versions, using the registry's existing extension point for structured
  metadata on model versions.
- Expose the run reference when model versions are retrieved through the
  Model Registry REST API.
- Keep model versions registered without a run reference valid (backward
  compatibility with existing registered models).
- The reference must identify the run sufficiently for a client in the same
  project to locate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a producing run, when the version is
  retrieved through the registry's REST API, then it carries a reference to
  that run.
- Given a model version registered without a run reference, retrieval
  succeeds without error (backward compatible).
- Given a model version's run reference, a client can resolve the referenced
  run within the same project (project and run identity are recoverable from
  the reference).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1), data side: registered model versions link back to the run that
  produced them.

# Open run comparisons from the Model Registry

## Description

From the Model Registry view in the Dashboard, users can open a run comparison
seeded with the run recorded as the producer of a selected registered model
version, connecting registry browsing to the run comparison workflow used for
model promotion decisions.

## Scope

- Entry point in the Dashboard's Model Registry section: from a registered
  model version that carries a producing-run reference, open the run
  comparison populated with that run, where additional runs can be selected
  alongside it.
- Graceful handling of registered model versions that carry no run reference.
- Reuses the run comparison view delivered for the runs-list workflow; this
  epic adds the registry entry surface and does not build a second comparison
  surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version with a recorded producing-run reference,
  when the user opens the comparison from the registry view, then the run
  comparison opens populated with that run and supports adding further runs
  to the selection.
- Given a registered model version without a run reference, the comparison
  entry point is unavailable or disabled with an explanatory state; no error
  is surfaced to the user.
- The comparison opened from the registry presents parameters, metrics, and
  diff behavior identically to the comparison reached from the runs list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1), UI side: a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry
  (the registry UI lives in the Dashboard).

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

Documentation for the run comparison workflow, covering both entry points:
selecting runs from the runs list and opening a comparison from the Model
Registry. Gives data scientists a reference for using comparison — including
the diff presentation — in model promotion decisions.

## Scope

Content outline (new/updated documentation topics):

- Selecting two or more training or pipeline runs from the runs list and
  reading the side-by-side parameters and metrics.
- Reading the diff highlighting between two selected runs.
- Opening a comparison from a registered model version in the Model Registry,
  including the behavior when a model version has no recorded run reference.
- Procedure steps and screenshots for both entry points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers the comparison workflow from the runs list, verified
  against the shipped behavior.
- Documentation covers the comparison workflow from the Model Registry,
  verified against the shipped behavior.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implementation before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.
